title: [NEXT-1122] Numeric Literals with Separators on `revalidate` Configuration throw TS Plugin Error

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

labels.name: linear: next
labels.description: Confirmed issue that is tracked by the Next.js team.

body:
### Verify canary release

- [X] I verified that the issue exists in the latest Next.js canary release

### Provide environment information

```bash
N/A
```


### Which area(s) of Next.js are affected? (leave empty if unsure)

TypeScript (plugin, built-in types)

### Link to the code that reproduces this issue

N/A

### To Reproduce

To reproduce this, simply export a `revalidate` option with a `_` separator in it:

```ts
export const revalidate = 86_400;
```

This creates an error because the TS Plugin:

https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/e6cfc155a70b5cfe2ac89d2233fda7738d1614d5/packages/next/src/server/typescript/rules/config.ts#L103

On this line, makes use of `Number`, but `Number` doesn't handle separators according to the spec. To handle this, the solution would be to replace it with:

```diff
-      return value === 'false' || Number(value) >= 0
+      return value === 'false' || Number(value.replaceAll("_", "")) >= 0
```

I haven't tested this solution, but it should fix the problem.

### Describe the Bug

The bug is that the export is highlighted with a invalid export type highlighted.

### Expected Behavior

The expected behavior is that an error is not shown.

### Which browser are you using? (if relevant)

Chrome

### How are you deploying your application? (if relevant)

Vercel
